without nausea, vomiting, chills, or fever

concepts.why: Elevated CA19-9 and CEA levels, along with a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa, suggest intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
Right upper abdominal tenderness, negative Murphy's sign, and gallbladder wall thickening indicate cholecystitis.
Gallstones are present, as indicated by ultrasonography and CT findings.

aliases: Enlarged lymph nodes in the liver hilum
concepts.why: Contrast-enhanced CT shows multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes, which may be related to intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
The patient has an elevated WBC count, indicating a possible inflammatory response.
Ultrasonography reveals enhanced pancreatic echogenicity, which may be related to gallstones or cholecystitis.

aliases: Slight dilation of the bile ducts in the liver
concepts.why: Liver MRI shows mild intrahepatic bile duct dilatation, which may be related to intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
The patient presents with a 2-month history of right upper abdominal pain.

rationales.F05: Right upper abdominal tenderness is a common symptom of cholecystitis and gallstones.

rationales.F09: Elevated CEA levels can be seen in various cancers, including intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
rationales.F10: Elevated CA19-9 levels are commonly seen in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
rationales.F11: Leukocytosis can be seen in various conditions, including cholecystitis and infections.
rationales.F12: A heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa is suggestive of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
